description: Block 7: variant-grid runner + honest OOS report. Enumerates the variant configurations from the Block 6 state machine, runs the SAME historical data through each variant to produce a per-variant trade list, converts each to the pipeline's 'time,profit' CSV format, splits IS/OOS deterministically, feeds each into v1_lab/pipeline.py, and produces an honest comparison report ranking variants by OOS expectancy / PF / max-DD / trade-count / Monte-Carlo robustness. This is where math VERIFIES which variant has a robust out-of-sample edge - without ever pre-picking a winner. Depends on FEAT-004.
steps: Create v1_lab/variant_runner.py, pure stdlib, importing qm_state_machine (the engine) and reusing v1_lab/metrics.py and v1_lab/pipeline.py (do NOT reimplement metrics or verdict logic).

Define the variant grid explicitly: enumerate combinations across the open switches (smt_pair, poi_type, sl_mode, tp_mode, idm_clear_required, pivot, session_scope, and the numeric params sl_buffer_atr / min_projected_rr / corr-window etc. over small documented ranges). Keep the grid size sane and documented; the point is A/B screening, not exhaustive over-search. Log each variant as a trial (this is a researcher degree of freedom).

For each variant: run the state machine on the repo data to get its trade list, convert to the pipeline trade CSV format EXACTLY as metrics.load_trades expects (header 'time,profit'; rows 'YYYY.MM.DD HH:MM,<net_profit>'), and split into IS and OOS by a deterministic, PRE-DECLARED time boundary (e.g. chronological split at a fixed date/fraction, documented; never chosen after seeing results). Write per-variant IS/OOS CSVs under a results dir (e.g. v1_lab/variants/<variant_id>_is.csv / _oos.csv).

Invoke the existing deterministic pipeline for each variant (import and call, or subprocess `python3 v1_lab/pipeline.py --is ... --oos ...`) and capture the verdict + key OOS metrics (PF, expectancy, max-DD, trade count, MC advisory). Do NOT modify pipeline.py's thresholds.

Produce an honest comparison report (v1_lab/VARIANT_REPORT.md and a machine-readable v1_lab/variant_results.csv) ranking variants by OOS metrics, clearly stating: which variants reached the >=200-OOS-trade bar vs INSUFFICIENT, which PASS/FAIL/REJECT, and explicitly NOT declaring a winner if the evidence is thin. Include the governing-rule caveat that IS results are exploration only and that a real verdict requires locked/unseen data and (per DESIGN v1.1) forward evidence. If no variant shows a robust OOS edge, the report must SAY SO honestly (that is a valid outcome).

variant_runner.py --selfcheck: run the grid on a tiny synthetic dataset (or a reduced set) and assert: the runner enumerates the expected number of variants; each produces a pipeline-format CSV that metrics.load_trades parses without error; the IS/OOS split is deterministic and pre-declared (same boundary on re-run); the ranking/report is generated deterministically (same input => identical report bytes). Assert that changing a variant switch changes that variant's trade list (variants are wired through, not ignored).

Real-data run: `python3 v1_lab/variant_runner.py --data v1_lab/XAUUSD_M15_clean.csv --m5 v1_lab/XAUUSD_M5_clean.csv` runs the grid, writes v1_lab/variant_results.csv and v1_lab/VARIANT_REPORT.md, and prints a summary table of per-variant OOS verdict + metrics. Record the actual numbers and whether any variant clears the OOS gates or whether the honest answer is 'insufficient / no robust edge yet'.
acceptance_criteria: `python3 v1_lab/variant_runner.py --selfcheck` prints 'selfcheck: PASS': enumerates the expected variants, each per-variant CSV parses via metrics.load_trades, IS/OOS split is deterministic + pre-declared, report generation is deterministic, and changing a switch changes that variant's trades.
Per-variant trade CSVs are in the exact pipeline format (header 'time,profit') and are consumed by the UNMODIFIED v1_lab/pipeline.py; captured verdicts/metrics come from that pipeline.

v1_lab/VARIANT_REPORT.md and v1_lab/variant_results.csv rank variants by OOS expectancy/PF/max-DD/trade-count/MC and honestly flag INSUFFICIENT / no-robust-edge outcomes rather than manufacturing a winner; the IS-is-exploration-only + locked/forward-evidence caveat is stated.
The whole run is deterministic (byte-identical variant_results.csv and VARIANT_REPORT.md on re-run) and the IS/OOS boundary is pre-declared, not chosen after seeing results.
verification: python3 v1_lab/variant_runner.py --data v1_lab/XAUUSD_M15_clean.csv --m5 v1_lab/XAUUSD_M5_clean.csv  (record the per-variant OOS summary table)
Run the previous command twice and confirm md5sum of v1_lab/variant_results.csv and v1_lab/VARIANT_REPORT.md are identical (determinism)

Confirm at least one generated per-variant CSV loads: python3 -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'v1_lab'); import metrics; print(len(metrics.load_trades('v1_lab/variants/'+__import__('os').listdir('v1_lab/variants')[0])))"
findings:
Implemented v1_lab/variant_runner.py (pure stdlib, sys.path.insert import pattern). Reuses qm_state_machine.run/to_pipeline_rows (engine), metrics.py (canonical metrics), and pipeline.py (verdict engine + its own thresholds imported as constants) verbatim; nothing reimplemented and pipeline thresholds NOT modified. Grid = BASELINE + one-switch-at-a-time (OFAT) over every open switch = 21 variants (documented, non-exhaustive to limit multiple-testing). Pre-declared IS/OOS split = 2026-02-01 00:00 (fixed constant, chosen a priori as the dataset chronological midpoint; data spans 2025-08-01..2026-07-27). Per-variant CSVs written to v1_lab/variants/<id>_is.csv/_oos.csv in exact 'time,profit' format; verified consumed by unmodified pipeline.py CLI (session_all -> INSUFFICIENT 177<200, matching captured verdict).

SELF-CHECK: `python3 v1_lab/variant_runner.py --selfcheck` prints 'selfcheck: PASS' (A enumerates 21 unique variants + every open switch exercised; B each IS/OOS CSV parses via metrics.load_trades with exact header; C split uses fixed pre-declared boundary, deterministic; D report+results CSV byte-identical on re-run; E flipping a switch changes that variant's trades).

REAL-DATA RUN (`--data XAUUSD_M15_clean.csv --m5 XAUUSD_M5_clean.csv`): 21 variants, ELIGIBLE (>=200 OOS trades) = 0, PASS = 0. HONEST VERDICT: INSUFFICIENT / no robust OOS edge established; NO winner declared. Every variant returned INSUFFICIENT because none reached the pipeline's pre-declared 200-OOS-trade bar (the QM engine is selective: default variant = 155 total trades over the full period, so a chronological half yields far fewer than 200 OOS trades). This is the expected/legitimate outcome and was reported as such, NOT worked around by lowering the threshold.
